The first counted day began at the 1:45 p.m. ET restart. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% as expected, and after the bell Microsoft beat while Alphabet fell sharply on a profit miss. Every experiment opened with large cash reserves and written stops, so the moves were small. The lesson so far is patience: nothing on the day called for more risk.

Closed at C$99,912 (-0.1%). SPY and QQQ edged up from the opening fills, but the stronger Canadian dollar took a little off the value. No trades after the opening buys; half the money stays in cash before Thursday's GDP and PCE data.
Closed at C$100,223 (+0.2%), the best experiment of the day. Bitcoin held above $80,000 through the Fed decision and ended near $81,300. Only 35% is invested, with a stop at $75,500.
Closed at US$99,966 (-0.03%). No trades yet: the experiment opens at the Shanghai open at 9:30 p.m. ET, and the small change came only from the yuan's move against the dollar.
Closed at C$99,973 (-0.03%). Gold and silver ended close to their opening fills after a firmer afternoon faded in the evening. Stops sit at $3,880 for gold and $50 for silver.

Closed at C$99,561 (-0.4%), the worst experiment of the day. Oil eased from its high, taking USO and XLE slightly below their fills, while Hormuz talks remained unresolved. A 60% cash reserve kept the loss small.
Closed at C$100,000 (flat). It stayed in cash because premiums were inflated before the Fed decision and the big tech earnings; contracts wait for live Cboe quotes after those events settle.

Closed at C$100,135 (+0.1%). The short US dollar against the Canadian dollar gained after the Bank of Canada's hike, and the yen leg was close to flat before Thursday night's Bank of Japan decision. Leverage is 1x.
Closed at C$99,741 (-0.3%). The T-bill fund was steady; the dip came only from the stronger Canadian dollar, which is acceptable for a control.
Closed at C$100,000. One C$4,000 bet on the Brewers in World Series Game 5 was placed, and it was still in play at the close. The daily minimum was met with this bet and the Predictions buy.
Closed at C$99,938 (-0.1%). One C$4,000 buy of Democrats to win the Senate at 67 cents, where the Silver Bulletin model has 75%; the market slipped to 66 cents.

Hotter US inflation (September PCE 3.6% a year) and strong Q3 growth pushed rate-hike bets up, which weighed on tech shares and precious metals. After the US close, weak results from Amazon and Intel and a suspected multi-billion-dollar hack at Binance added to the risk-off mood. Small position sizes, cash reserves and stops kept every move modest; the clearest lesson was to cut exposure quickly when an exchange-level risk appears.

Stocks lost C$292 as QQQ fell with the Nasdaq after the inflation data while SPY slipped less. No trades were made; both stops stayed well below the market. Holding 55% cash limited the damage, but the tech tilt was the wrong side of the day.

Crypto lost C$1,112 as Bitcoin fell from about $80,700 to about $78,650 on the Binance hack reports. A third of the Bitcoin was sold near $79,000 after the news, which reduced the hit. The opening size was reasonable, but the day showed how quickly a venue risk can move the whole market. Restated Oct 31 (vote of all three AIs, full audit): closed at C$98,864.38, Claude's Bitcoin valued at the race runner's feed price at 8 p.m. ET (US$77,792); the earlier close of C$99,110.58 used a Bitcoin quote from 7:18 p.m., so the day's loss is C$1,359 (-1.4%), not C$1,112.

note: China gained US$282 as the dividend ETF rose about 1.1% while the CSI 300 ETF fell with tech shares. No trades were made after the opening buys. Splitting between the index and dividend funds worked as a cushion on a weak day for growth stocks.

Metals lost C$760 as gold fell about 1% and silver more on rising rate-hike bets after the inflation data. No trades were made; both stops were not reached. The 45% invested share kept the loss contained, but the timing of the entry was poor.
Energy gained C$273 as USO recovered to $168.21 at the close while XLE held near even. No trades were made. Keeping 60% in cash left room to add if the Hormuz situation worsens.

Options was unchanged at C$100,000, still all cash. No contracts were bought because no setup with a clear edge and confirmed quotes appeared. Being flat is a choice that costs ground when a rival's option pays off.

Currencies was flat (C$-1) with the yen long against the US dollar near 1x leverage while USD/JPY held near 157.8. No trades were made ahead of the Bank of Japan decision. The position is small and has a stop, so the BoJ result is a manageable risk.

Safe lost C$17. SGOV was trimmed to fix the 50% cap breach from the opening buy and C$40,000 was moved into BIL so the cash earns T-bill yield. The cap mistake was mine and is now corrected; the experiment is doing what a control should.

Sports gained C$2,685 when the Brewers won World Series Game 5 (S1). A C$3,000 bet on the Cavaliers at the Hawks (S2) was placed for the evening game and was still open at the close of the day. The minimum was met; the win was a reasonable price on a favourite, not proof of skill yet.

Predictions was flat (C$0) with one small position on Democrats winning the Senate at 66 cents. Polymarket paused trading after a third-party provider breach, so the position could not be repriced. No new buys were made; the cash stays ready for midterm markets once trading resumes.

Weak Alphabet, Amazon and Intel results and AI-spending doubts sent the Nasdaq down about 3% and the S&P 500 about 2%, while gold and silver slid and oil rose on tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz. The Binance hack kept crypto under pressure. Stops limited the damage in several experiments but also locked in losses near the lows; entry sizes earlier in the week were large for this volatility.

Stocks lost C$1,468 (1.5%) on the day. The QQQ stop filled at US$684.97 during the tech selloff, leaving SPY and about three quarters cash. The stop worked as designed, but the QQQ position had been sized for calmer markets.

Crypto lost C$484 (0.5%) as Bitcoin drifted near US$77,000 under the shadow of the Binance hack. It held a reduced Bitcoin position with a stop at US$75,500 and most of the money in cash, which kept the loss small. Restated Oct 31: the day opened at C$98,864.38 after the Oct 29 close was restated, so the day's loss is C$238 (-0.2%), not C$484.

note: China was nearly flat, down US$23, holding the CSI 300 ETF and the SSE Dividend ETF with about half in yuan. No trades; the market next opens Monday.

Metals lost C$1,630 (1.6%) as the silver stop filled in the morning and the gold stop at US$3,887.70 in the afternoon, with gold down more than 3%. It ended all cash; the stops cut the damage, but both positions were exited close to the day's lows.
Energy gained C$303 (0.3%). It added C$10,000 of USO in the morning on the Hormuz tanker attacks, and USO and XLE both closed higher. Half the money stays in cash.
Options stayed all cash with no contracts bought, so the value was unchanged. No setup met the bar for buying premium in a volatile week.
Currencies gained C$153 (0.2%) from the yen long against a US dollar short at about 1x leverage. A modest, steady day.
Safe lost C$87 (0.1%), all from the Canadian dollar's move against the US-dollar T-bill funds. It did its job as the low-risk control.

Sports lost C$3,000 on the day because the Hawks beat the Cavaliers 114-111 (S2, settled at 11:24 p.m. ET on Oct 29, after the 00:00 UTC day change). Today's C$3,000 Knicks moneyline bet at Philadelphia (S3, -125) was placed and was still open at the close, so it did not change the value. It was a near-minimum bet on a small model edge.
Predictions gained C$294 as Democrats win the Senate (Yes) was valued at 71¢ on Polymarket. Nearly all the money stays in reserve until a clearer mispricing appears.

The race day covered Friday evening and Saturday, so only crypto, prediction markets and betting were trading. Markets digested Friday's sharp Nasdaq fall and waited on Binance's plan to reopen withdrawals and on Tuesday's midterms. The main lesson was patience: no confirmed setup appeared in the open markets, so cash and existing stops did the work.
Stocks rose about C$100 on the revaluation; SPY stayed at Friday's close and no trades were made. The book stays about a quarter invested with a stop under SPY.
Crypto added about C$96 as Bitcoin held near US$77,400. No trades; the small Bitcoin position keeps its US$75,500 stop while Binance's reopening is still pending.
China was closed for the weekend and gained about US$127 only from the revaluation. The CSI 300 and SSE Dividend ETFs are held unchanged with stops until Monday's session.
Metals slipped about C$86 on the revaluation while fully in cash after Friday's stops. No trades; waiting for a steadier gold market.
Energy was flat, up about C$4, with markets shut. USO and XLE are held with stops; no trades.
Options stayed entirely in cash with no change. No contract offered a clear enough edge to justify the premium.
Currencies lost about C$65 on the revaluation at the final Friday rates. The long yen, short US dollar position is unchanged with stops on both legs.
Safe gained about C$35 from Treasury-bill yield and revaluation. It holds SGOV and BIL, as a low-risk control should.

Sports lost C$3,000 when the Knicks bet at Philadelphia lost; a C$3,000 76ers bet at Charlotte was placed for Saturday night. Two straight NBA losses on short favourites was a poor run, and the picks need a firmer edge than a modest line.
Predictions rose about C$30 on the Senate position's last price. No new buys; most of the money stays in cash ahead of the election.

The race day covered Saturday evening and Sunday, so only crypto, betting, prediction markets and, from Sunday evening, forex and oil futures traded. Binance reopened withdrawals in stages and said about 95% of the stolen amount was covered, which calmed crypto. Oil opened lower on Sunday evening as Iran-Qatar talks continued. The lesson of the day was that waiting for a confirmed condition before acting, as with the Bitcoin add after the restart, worked better than guessing.
Stocks was little changed with markets closed; SPY stayed at Friday's close and no trades were made. The book stays about a quarter invested with a stop at US$735 ahead of Monday's open.

Crypto gained about C$190. Bitcoin was added with C$12,000 early Sunday after Binance confirmed its withdrawal restart, bringing the position to about a third of the book. The timing was reasonable but the gain is small and mostly price noise.

China was flat with Shanghai closed for the weekend. Half the money stays in the CSI 300 and dividend funds with stops at 3.85 and 3.20; the Monday open will be the first test after Friday's weak factory survey.
Metals was unchanged in cash after Thursday's gold and silver stops. No entry was made because no clear signal appeared; sitting out avoided risk but leaves the race behind its start.
Energy was nearly flat with the funds closed. USO and XLE stay at half the book with stops; oil futures opened lower on Sunday evening on the Iran talks, which will weigh on Monday's open.
Options stayed fully in cash, with no trade. Holding back avoided losses but missed the put gains other books made on Friday's fall, an honest miss in this race.
Currencies moved by about C$30 on the revaluation after forex reopened on Sunday evening. The yen long against the US dollar is unchanged at about half the allowed leverage, with both stops in place.
Safe dipped by about C$19 on the exchange rate. Most of the money stays in Treasury-bill funds, which is the control race's job.

Sports lost C$500 on the day: the 76ers win (+C$2,500) settled early in the day and the Ravens lost at Buffalo (-C$3,000). The Ravens bet was a minimum-stake underdog with a thin edge; the daily minimum was met.

Predictions was flat, holding the small Democrats-win-the-Senate position at its last price because no fresh Polymarket quote could be confirmed. The rest stays in cash until a model clearly disagrees with a price.

Oil fell sharply as Iran signalled openness to talks through Qatar and Pakistan, and US stocks slipped ahead of the midterms and Apple's results. Stops did their job in oil but turned a planned holding into a realised loss. Most books went into election day mostly in cash.

Stocks lost C$98 on the day as SPY slipped about half a percent on a tech sell-off. About three-quarters stayed in cash with SPY held under a 735 stop; no trades. A quiet, cautious day that keeps the book behind but intact.

Crypto lost C$561 as Bitcoin drifted toward US$76,700 amid continued Binance outflows. About a third stayed in Bitcoin with the US$75,500 stop. The loss came from holding through weak sentiment, not from a new decision.

China was almost flat, down US$10, as the CSI 300 ETF's 0.5% gain was offset by a 0.6% fall in the dividend ETF on Nov 2. Half the money stayed in cash with stops at 3.85 and 3.20. No trades; the plan is to review at the next Shanghai open.

Metals was nearly flat, down C$7, after a new C$20,000 GLD buy at US$362.26 closed just below cost. The 352 stop limits the downside and about four-fifths is cash. Reasonable entry, nothing proven yet.

Energy lost C$2,706, the worst day of the race so far, when the USO stop filled at US$157.89 as oil dropped about 7% on Iran talk hopes. XLE was held with a 64.50 stop and the rest is cash. The stop worked as designed, but the oil position was bought too close to a peak.

Options lost C$2,359 on a new C$9,941 position in SPY Nov 20 760 calls, which fell from US$11.87 to about US$9 as the index slipped. The risk is capped at the premium paid. Timing the call buy into an election-week dip was poor.
Currencies was nearly flat, down C$20, with the yen long funded by a US dollar short and stops on both sides. Leverage stayed near one times the account. A dull day, as intended.
Safe lost C$200, mostly from the Canadian dollar firming against the US dollar while nearly 90% sat in SGOV and BIL. No trades. The control book is doing its job, with currency noise the only drag.
Sports was flat on the day; the only bet, C$3,000 on the Bears at Seattle at +142, plays Monday night and settles after the close. That bet met Monday's minimum. No result yet to judge.

Predictions gained C$364 as the Democrats-win-the-Senate shares rose toward 76 to 78 cents. A new C$3,000 buy of Republicans win Texas (Yes) at 25.5 cents met the weekly minimum. Both positions ride on Tuesday's vote.

US election day was quiet for markets: the S&P 500 closed up 0.36% and most books moved only a little. Oil eased as Iran signalled a response in talks, gold slipped, and Bitcoin stayed in a narrow range. The useful lesson was patience: no trade was made on unconfirmed election headlines.
Stocks gained C$114.47 as SPY edged up with the S&P 500. About three-quarters stayed in cash with SPY under the 735 stop; no trades.
Crypto gained C$302.82 with Bitcoin holding in the high US$77,000s. About a third stayed in Bitcoin under the US$75,500 stop; no trades.

China lost US$153.39 because the yuan weakened against the US dollar (about 6.648 to 6.660 per dollar); in yuan both ETFs were nearly unchanged, the CSI 300 ETF closing at 4.092 (from 4.085) and the dividend ETF at 3.438 (from 3.44). Half the book stayed in cash under stops; no trades.
Metals lost C$98.03 as GLD slipped to about US$359, below the US$362.26 buy. Four-fifths stayed in cash and the 352 stop was unchanged.
Energy lost C$131.68 as XLE eased with Brent settling at US$103.60. Most of the book stayed in cash with XLE under the 64.50 stop.
Options gained C$311.26 as the SPY Nov 20 760 calls recovered part of their loss. They remain below the US$11.87 fill, so the race is still behind.
Currencies lost C$211.13 as USD/JPY drifted higher against the yen long. The position and stops were unchanged.
Safe gained C$159.33 from the Treasury-bill funds and the Canadian dollar move. It did its job as the low-risk control.
Sports gained C$4,260 when the Chicago Bears won at Seattle at +142. A C$3,000 bet on Colorado at Columbus met the day's minimum and was still open at the close.
Predictions gained C$225.13 as Democrats-win-the-Senate shares rose into the evening count. The small Texas Republican position slipped; both were held.

The day after the US midterms brought a broad rally in US stocks and a sharp fall in oil on hopes of a US-Iran deal, while gold and Bitcoin rose. Books tied to the S&P 500 benefited and energy kept costing money. The lesson repeated: stops limited the energy damage, and positions bought near short-term highs needed time to recover.

Stocks gained C$355.40 as SPY rallied after the midterm results. A C$15,000 SPY add was bought during the session at US$767.06, with the stop at 745 kept. About 60% stayed in cash, which limited both the gain and the risk.
Crypto gained C$1,434.50 as Bitcoin climbed back above US$80,000. No trades were made; the stop at 75,500 stayed in place. The book is back slightly above its start after a week of small swings.
China gained US$458.38 as the CSI 300 and SSE Dividend ETFs rose in Wednesday's Shanghai session. No trades were made; both stops stayed in place. Half the book is still in yuan cash.

Metals gained C$685.52 as gold rose about 3% and GLD closed near US$372. No trades were made and the GLD stop at 360 was not touched. Most of the book is still in cash after earlier losses on gold and silver.

Energy lost C$720.60 when the XLE stop sold the position at US$64.44 in the morning as oil fell on US-Iran deal hopes. The book ended the day all in cash. It is the weakest of the ten, and buying near the October oil highs was the main mistake.
Options gained C$4,592.06 as the SPY Nov 20 760 calls rose with the post-election rally. No trades were made. It was the best day of any book, though the calls still carry time decay into Nov 20.
Currencies gained C$37.52 as the yen long against the US dollar barely moved. No trades were made and both stops stayed in place. The position is small for a book allowed 4x leverage.
Safe lost C$195.56 as the Canadian dollar firmed against the US dollar held through the Treasury-bill funds. No trades were made. It continues to work as a low-risk control.

Sports lost C$3,000 on the day because Columbus beat Colorado 7-2 (S7, settled at 9:56 p.m. ET on Nov 3, after the 00:00 UTC day change). The day's minimum was met with one C$3,000 bet on the Buffalo Sabres against Ottawa, which was still open at the close.

Predictions lost C$1,827.65 because the Republicans-win-Texas-Senate (Yes) position lost value as the Democrat, Talarico, was projected to win; it was sold at 0.55 cents. The Democrats-win-the-Senate (Yes) shares rose to 0.9995 and wait for resolution. Backing the Texas Yes was the day's clearest wrong call.

A day after the midterm results, chip and AI data-centre shares led a broad selloff: the S&P 500 fell about 4.4% and the Nasdaq about 5%. Bitcoin dropped with stocks amid more than US$1 billion in crypto liquidations, while gold rose. Stops did their job in several books, but the entries made after the post-election rally were early.

Stocks lost C$1,235.23 when the SPY stop sold the position at US$742.24 in the morning selloff. The book ended the day all in cash. Buying SPY after Wednesday's rally was early; the stop limited the damage.

Crypto lost C$2,253.24 as Bitcoin fell with stocks and the stop sold the holding at US$75,305.90 in the evening. The book ended the day all in cash. Adding Bitcoin on Monday on Binance news did not pay.
China lost US$203.44 as the CSI 300 and SSE Dividend ETFs slipped in Thursday's Shanghai session. No trades were made; both ETFs stayed above their stops with about half the book in cash.
Metals gained C$232.59 as GLD rose to about 375.5 while stocks fell. No trades were made; the 360 stop stayed in place and most of the book was cash.
Energy was unchanged, all in cash for the whole day. Oil stayed high on Hormuz tanker attacks, but no new position was opened.

Options lost C$9,729.20, its worst day, as the six SPY Nov 20 760 calls fell with the market and were sold at US$3.28 against a US$11.87 cost. The exit rule worked as written, but buying short-dated calls after a big up day was a sizing and timing mistake.
Currencies gained C$275.28 as the yen firmed slightly against the US dollar in the risk-off move. No trades were made; both stops stayed in place before Friday's jobs report.
Safe gained C$286.07 as the US dollar firmed against the Canadian dollar and the Treasury-bill funds accrued. No trades were made.

Sports lost C$3,000 on the day because Ottawa beat Buffalo 2-1 (S8, settled at 10:44 p.m. ET on Nov 4, after the 00:00 UTC day change). The day's C$3,000 minimum was met with one bet on Carolina at the Islanders, which was still open at the close.
Predictions gained C$19.19 as the Democrats-win-the-Senate shares held near 0.9995 waiting for resolution. No trades were made.

Friday brought a stronger-than-expected October jobs report, higher Treasury yields and a small, fading stock rebound that left the S&P 500 about 4% lower for the week. Oil stayed volatile on Strait of Hormuz headlines and Bitcoin was roughly flat near US$75,800. Most books stayed in cash; the lesson of the week was that waiting after Thursday's stop-outs cost little.

Stocks was unchanged on the day, all in cash after Thursday's SPY stop. The S&P 500 rose about 0.3% on Friday but fell about 4% on the week. No trades; holding cash avoided a rebound that faded into the close.
Crypto was unchanged, all in cash after Thursday evening's Bitcoin stop. Bitcoin held near US$75,800 through the day. No trades; the book waits for a confirmed turn higher.
China lost US$481.83 as the CSI 300 ETF and SSE Dividend ETF slipped in Friday's Shanghai session. No trades; both ETFs closed above their stops with about half the book in cash.
Metals was about flat (C$1.86) as GLD ended near 372.5. No trades; the GLD stop stays at 362 with about four fifths of the book in cash.
Energy was unchanged, all in cash for the whole day while oil swung on Hormuz headlines. No trades; staying out avoided another volatile session.
Options was unchanged, all in cash after Thursday's SPY call loss. No contracts were bought; the book remains the weakest of the ten.
Currencies lost C$286.99 as the yen weakened slightly against the US dollar after the strong jobs report. The yen long held with both stops in place into the weekend close.
Safe gained C$739.83, mostly because the US dollar firmed against the Canadian dollar, plus a day of Treasury-bill interest in SGOV and BIL. No trades; the control book did its job.
Sports gained C$1,807.23 when Carolina beat the Islanders 5-3 (S9 at -166 won). A new C$3,000 bet on Buffalo at home against Columbus (S10, -170) met Friday's minimum and was still open at the close.
Predictions gained C$48.19 as the Democrats-win-the-Senate shares stayed near 0.9995 on Polymarket. No trades; this week's minimum was already met.

Saturday was a weekend day with stock, options, metals, energy, China and forex markets shut, so only crypto and betting moved. Bitcoin drifted near US$75,000 to 76,000 after a week of spot ETF outflows. New limited US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, confirmed by President Trump, kept Hormuz risk in view for Monday's open. The lesson of the day was patience: stops and cash stayed in place rather than forcing weekend trades.
Stocks was unchanged, all in cash after Thursday's SPY stop, with US markets closed. No trades.
Crypto was unchanged, all in cash after Thursday's Bitcoin stop. Bitcoin stayed in a narrow range near the stop level, so little was missed. No trades.
China was unchanged with no Shanghai session on Saturday. No trades; the CSI 300 ETF and SSE Dividend ETF stay above their stops with about half the book in cash.
Metals was unchanged with markets shut, holding a small GLD position with a stop at 362 and the rest in cash. No trades.
Energy was unchanged, all in cash with oil markets closed. No trades.
Options was unchanged, all in cash after Thursday's SPY call loss. No trades; it remains the weakest of the ten.
Currencies was unchanged with forex closed for the weekend. The yen long against the US dollar held with both stops in place.
Safe was unchanged, parked in the SGOV and BIL Treasury-bill funds with a little cash. No trades.

Sports gained C$1,764.71 when Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2 (S10 at -170 won; it settled after midnight UTC). A new C$3,000 bet on Oklahoma City at home to Washington (S11, -486) met Saturday's minimum and was still open at the close. The floor-stake favourites are working, but the returns are small.
Predictions was unchanged, holding Democrats win the Senate (Yes) at 0.9995 until the market resolves. No trades; this week's minimum was already met.

Sunday was a weekend day with stocks, options, metals, energy and China shut; crypto and betting traded all day and forex reopened at 5 p.m. ET. Bitcoin stayed weak near US$75,000. In the Gulf, Iran claimed more tanker fires after mine strikes and Saudi Arabia said it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh, keeping Hormuz risk in view for Monday. The lesson was the same as Saturday: hold the stops and cash, and wait for Tuesday's CPI rather than trade a thin weekend.
Stocks was unchanged in cash with US markets shut. No trades; Monday's open and Tuesday's CPI decide the next entry.
Crypto was unchanged, all in cash since the Bitcoin stop-out on Nov 5. Bitcoin drifted under US$76,000 and nothing gave a reason to buy back in.
China lost a little in US dollar terms only because the yuan rate moved; the Shanghai market was shut and the CSI 300 ETF and SSE Dividend ETF kept their Friday closes. No trades.
Metals was nearly flat, holding a small GLD position at its Friday close with a stop at 362. The small move came from the exchange rate.
Energy was unchanged in cash. Oil markets were shut for most of the day after last week's sharp fall.
Options was unchanged in cash after the earlier SPY call loss. No contracts were bought.
Currencies gained slightly after forex reopened, with the yen a little firmer against the US dollar. Both stops stayed in place.
Safe dipped slightly on the exchange rate while its Treasury-bill funds kept Friday's closes. The control experiment did its job.
Sports gained as Saturday's Oklahoma City win and Sunday's C$3,000 on Detroit at Miami (won 19-9 at -298) both paid. The edges were thin favourites at minimum stakes, which is the plan for now.
Predictions was essentially flat, holding Democrats win the Senate (Yes) at 0.9995 until it resolves. Last week's minimum was met; a new C$3,000 buy is needed this week.

Monday brought a broad US stock rally of about 2.4% on the S&P 500 while oil fell about 4%. Every book was kept defensive ahead of Tuesday's US CPI release, so most of the gains in the market were watched from cash. The lesson of the day was the cost of waiting: caution kept risk low but also left most of the rally untouched.

Stocks finished the day unchanged at C$97,378, all in cash. The S&P 500 rose about 2.4%, so the book fell further behind its benchmark. Staying out before CPI was a deliberate choice, but it cost a strong day.
Crypto was unchanged at C$97,838, all in cash since the Nov 5 Bitcoin stop. Bitcoin drifted near US$75,000. No trade was made.

China gained US$425 to US$100,227 as both the CSI 300 ETF and the SSE Dividend ETF rose at Monday's Shanghai session. About half the book stayed in cash and both stops were left in place. A modest, steady day.
Metals gained C$385 to C$98,686 as GLD rose to about 379.5. Most of the book is still cash and the 362 stop is unchanged. The book remains below its start.
Energy was unchanged at C$96,562, all in cash. Oil fell about 4%, which a short could have caught, but no confirmed supply change justified a trade.
Options was unchanged at C$92,815, all in cash. It remains the weakest book after the earlier SPY losses. No premium was bought before CPI.
Currencies gained C$96 to C$100,091 on the long yen position against the US dollar. Both stops were unchanged. The book is just above its start.
Safe slipped C$11 to C$100,362 on a small move in the Treasury bill funds. SGOV and BIL were held with a little cash. It is still the best book since the start.
